000.author: Becker, Joel et al.
000.title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
000.primary_topic: A randomized controlled trial of 16 experienced open-source developers on 246 real tasks finds early-2025 AI tools increased completion time by 19%, while developers and experts expected large speedups, revealing a gap between perceived and actual impact.

001.author: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
001.title: Secure Software Development Attestation Form Instructions
001.primary_topic: The common federal form, with instructions, by which a software producer's CEO or designee attests to consistent use of four SSDF-derived secure development practices before agencies may use its software, with third-party assessment and POA&M alternatives.

002.author: Cucumber (Aslak Hellesøy and contributors)
002.title: Cucumber documentation: Behaviour-Driven Development and the Gherkin reference
002.primary_topic: Presents BDD as a collaborative, example-driven practice run in the order Discovery, Formulation, Automation, with Gherkin as the human- and machine-readable medium for behaviour scenarios, and specifies Gherkin's keywords, step arguments, localisation and step organisation.

003.author: DORA (Google Cloud)
003.title: State of AI-assisted Software Development
003.primary_topic: Finds from a global survey and interviews that AI amplifies an organisation's existing strengths and dysfunctions, so its value depends on the surrounding system, and names seven capabilities, including quality platforms and small batches, that amplify AI's benefits.

004.author: Egashira, Kazuki et al.
004.title: TestSuiteBench: Coding Agents Struggle to Generate Strong Test Suites from Specifications
004.primary_topic: Introduces TestSuiteBench, 165 applications with specifications, reference implementations and isolated mutants, and shows frontier coding agents write valid but weak test suites from specifications, so they can build software they cannot verify.

005.author: He, Hao et al.
005.title: Speed at the Cost of Quality: How Cursor AI Increases Short-Term Velocity and Long-Term Complexity in Open-Source Projects
005.primary_topic: A staggered difference-in-differences study of open-source GitHub projects finding that Cursor adoption brings a large but transient velocity gain and persistent rises in static analysis warnings and code complexity that later slow velocity.

006.author: Jimenez, Carlos E. et al.
006.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
006.primary_topic: Builds SWE-bench, 2,294 real GitHub issues from 12 Python repositories scored by running tests on model-written patches, and finds models resolve only the simplest issues, with the best, Claude 2, solving 1.96%.

007.author: Microsoft (Industry Solutions Engineering)
007.title: Code-With Engineering Playbook
007.primary_topic: Practice guidance holding that code without tests is incomplete, laying out a pyramid of testing techniques, peer review of every pull request, team-agreed definitions of done and ready, and measurable, testable non-functional requirements.

008.author: Booth, Harold et al.
008.title: Secure Software Development Practices for Generative AI and Dual-Use Foundation Models: An SSDF Community Profile
008.primary_topic: A NIST SSDF Community Profile that augments SSDF 1.1 practices and tasks with AI-specific recommendations, priorities and references to address novel risks in generative AI and dual-use foundation model development across the lifecycle.

009.author: Souppaya, Murugiah; Scarfone, Karen; Dodson, Donna
009.title: Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) Version 1.1: Recommendations for Mitigating the Risk of Software Vulnerabilities
009.primary_topic: Argues for integrating outcome-based secure development practices, grouped as Prepare, Protect, Produce and Respond, into any existing software life cycle, tailored by risk rather than followed as a checklist, to reduce vulnerabilities and their recurrence.

00a.author: OpenSSF / Wheeler et al.
00a.title: Finding and Fixing Software Vulnerabilities Using AI: A Guide for Developers
00a.primary_topic: A developer guide arguing that AI-accelerated attacks demand AI-assisted vulnerability finding and fixing, done through disciplined processes (sandboxing, separate validation, triage, human review, durable checks) built on unchanged secure-development principles.

00b.author: OWASP GenAI Security Project, Agentic Security Initiative / Sotiropoulos et al.
00b.title: Agentic AI - Threats and Mitigations
00b.primary_topic: Builds a reference architecture for LLM-based agents and a threat model of seventeen agentic threats, new or amplified by memory, tools and autonomy, organised by a taxonomy navigator and answered with six mitigation playbooks.

00c.author: OWASP GenAI Security Project, Agentic Security Initiative / Sotiropoulos et al.
00c.title: OWASP Top 10 For Agentic Applications 2026
00c.primary_topic: Names the ten highest-impact security threats to agentic applications, from goal hijack to rogue agents, each with examples, attack scenarios and mitigations, arguing that agents amplify existing vulnerabilities and calling for least agency and strong observability.

00d.author: OWASP Foundation / Lang et al.
00d.title: OWASP Application Security Verification Standard 5.0.0
00d.primary_topic: Sets out 345 verifiable application security requirements in 17 chapters, framed as security goals rather than mechanisms, sorted into three risk-based levels and paired with documented security decisions, with guidance on verification and certification.

00e.author: OWASP GenAI Security Project / Wilson et al.
00e.title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2026
00e.primary_topic: Ranks ten LLM application security risks for 2026 by weighting a practitioner vote against real incident data, and argues that since models will be fooled, systems must be built so nothing important breaks when they are.

00f.author: UK Government Analysis Function
00f.title: The AQuA Book: The Analytical Quality Assurance Book (2025 edition)
00f.primary_topic: UK government guidance arguing that all analysis shall be independently assured, proportionately to business risk and complexity, through verification, validation and uncertainty handling across four roles and four life-cycle stages, backed by a strong quality assurance culture.

00g.author: UK Government Analytical Community
00g.title: Quality assurance of code for analysis and research
00g.primary_topic: UK government guidance adapting software engineering practices for analysts writing code, grounded in reproducible, auditable and assured analysis, applied proportionately to risk, and extended to reviewing LLM-generated code.

00h.author: Kalai, Adam Tauman; Nachum, Ofir; Vempala, Santosh S.; Zhang, Edwin
00h.title: Why Language Models Hallucinate
00h.primary_topic: Explains language-model hallucinations through a two-stage account: statistical generation errors during pretraining, formalised by an Is-It-Valid classification reduction and arbitrary-fact/poor-model lower bounds; and post-training persistence caused by mainstream binary evaluations that reward guessing and penalise abstention, with explicit confidence targets proposed as a mitigation.
